Incident history (37)

📅 2025-08-02 Artillery Shelling INC-243
PRCS headquarters in Khan Younis were shelled resulting in 1 death, 3 injuries, and a fire breaking out

The administrative headquarters of Al-Amal City, affiliated with the PRCS in Khan Yunis and located next to Al-Amal Hospital, was directly hit by Israeli artillery fire, resulting in the death of one of the society's cadres, Omar Mansour Hamdan Salim, and the injury of a number of employees, in addition to severe material damage. The PRCS stated that the first shell targeted the upper floors of the building, followed by a second shell while employees were inspecting the damage, and then a third shell targeted the first floor during attempts to extinguish the fire, indicating repeated targeting of the site during rescue operations.

📅 2024-03-23 – 2024-03-25 Invasion / Ground Assault INC-040
Israeli military has forced hospital staff and wounded patients to evacuate Al-Amal Hospital and closed the entrances with dirt barriers, the hospital is no longer operational.

In Khan Younis, amid intensive military operations, the Israeli military has forced hospital staff and wounded patients to evacuate Al-Amal Hospital using smoke bombs, they have also closed the hospital gate and block roads with dirt barriers, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS). Starting on the night of 24 March, staff and patients were stuck in ambulances outside the hospital for 20 hours due to the damage to roads around the hospital and dirt barriers that the IDF built. When two individuals tried to move debris from the road they were fired at by IDF soldiers (PRCS on X). On 25 March, PRCS, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), and OCHA evacuated six patients and a companion, 27 staff, and retrieved the bodies of two people who were killed inside the hospital, including a PRCS volunteer who was a member of the Emergency Operations Room. As of 26 March, both the hospital and the nearby PRCS headquarters have ceased functioning. On the same day, IFRC issued a statement, emphasizing that sustained hostilities in and around Al-Amal Hospital for over 40 days have placed PRCS teams and patients in grave danger, and that the “forced closure of Al-Amal Hospital, one of the few remaining medical facilities in the south [and the second PRCS hospital to shut down], has profound implications, leaving countless lives at risk.” [OCHA Flash Update #147]

📅 2024-01-21 – 2024-03-25 Siege INC-241
Siege by israeli military lasting from January to March of 2024, PRCS reported that 27 individuals died over the course of the seige

Israeli forces besieged Al-Amal hospital and the PRCS headquarters from January to March of 2024. Many sources split this siege into two seperate events, the first spanning from 22 Jan 2024, to 9 Feb 2024 when IDF forces raided the hospital, and then a second siege starting in early to mid Feb 2024 and lasting until 25 March 2024. Access to the hospital was restricted, leading to danger to patients and staff. The siege also prevented the movement of supplies into the hospital, resulting in shortages of oxygen, blood, and medical supplies as well as food, water, and fuel. By the end of the siege patients and staff were forced to evacuate the building and Al-Amal was no longer operational. PRCS reported that 27 individuals died during the siege; those individuals deaths have been recorded on the specific dates and with the specific indcidents that led to their deaths. Over the course of the siege, Al-Amal continued to be targeted by shelling, gunfire, invasions, and other violence.

📅 2024-01-03 vicinity bombed INC-041
3rd consecutive day of bombardment in area of Al-Amal hospital resulting in multiple deaths and injuires, and damage to communications

PRCS reported that seven IDPs sheltering in the compound, including a five-day-old baby, had been killed [five deaths, including the baby happened on 2 Jan, 2 other deaths occured on 3 or 4 Jan], while another 11 people were injured over the three days of bombardment [ 3 people injured on 2 Jan, 8 other injuries occured on 3 or 4 Jan]. 📅 2023-11-11 – 2023-11-14 siege INC-022
For three consecutive days the main generator shut down due to lack of fuel.

For three consecutive days, the main generator at Al-Amal hospital in Khan Younis shut down due to lack of fuel. INC-241📅 2024-01-21 – 2024-03-25Siege
×

Siege by israeli military lasting from January to March of 2024, PRCS reported that 27 individuals died over the course of the seige

📍 Al-Amal Hospital — Khan Younis, Khan Younis

Summary

Israeli forces besieged Al-Amal hospital and the PRCS headquarters from January to March of 2024. Many sources split this siege into two seperate events, the first spanning from 22 Jan 2024, to 9 Feb 2024 when IDF forces raided the hospital, and then a second siege starting in early to mid Feb 2024 and lasting until 25 March 2024. Access to the hospital was restricted, leading to danger to patients and staff. The siege also prevented the movement of supplies into the hospital, resulting in shortages of oxygen, blood, and medical supplies as well as food, water, and fuel. By the end of the siege patients and staff were forced to evacuate the building and Al-Amal was no longer operational. PRCS reported that 27 individuals died during the siege; those individuals deaths have been recorded on the specific dates and with the specific indcidents that led to their deaths. Over the course of the siege, Al-Amal continued to be targeted by shelling, gunfire, invasions, and other violence.

Sources
